titleEn: Toes Out, Side by Side—Slip In!

pages.text: At the evening doorway, Dad turned each guest's shoes with toes facing out. Kota tossed off wooden clogs and ran onto the porch. One lay here, the other there.
In the morning, Kota searched ages for one clog. Finding it at last, Kota put it on backward and waddled. "I hate these shoes!" Kota pouted.
A long-snouted boar arrived and tossed off his shoes. "I leave early tomorrow for the dawn market." His shoes scattered like Kota's.
That evening, Dad gave Kota one clog. "Shall we put shoes to bed? Toes Out, Side by Side—Slip In!" Kota tilted their head. "Do shoes sleep?"
Kota set both clogs together, turning their toes toward the yard. A foot slipped right in! "Wow, I can put them on without looking!"
"Let's put our guest's shoes to bed, too." Kota picked them up and set them side by side on the stepping stone, toes both facing the yard.
Before dawn, still dim, the boar stretched out his feet. They slipped right into his shoes. "My feet found their own way!" Watching through the door, Kota's tail shot up.
"Thank you, little shoe captain!" He stroked Kota's head. Kota blushed. The boar strode cheerfully into the dawn.
Now, every time Kota climbed onto the porch, fingers counted: "One, side by side! Two, toes out! Three, slip in!" Shoes lined the doorway neatly each evening.
At night, shoes rested side by side, toes out. Dad hugged Kota. "Getting ready ahead makes morning smile." "Tomorrow morning, Toes Out, Side by Side—Slip In!"
